title: Grade 6 Math — Tue, Jun 17
description: Triangles — Day 2 of 5: Types by angles and angle sum property
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is ___.
questions.explanation: Angle sum property: the three interior angles of every triangle always add up to 180°.

questions.question: A triangle with all three angles less than 90° is called ___.
questions.explanation: An acute triangle has all three interior angles less than 90°.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has exactly ___ right angle(s).
questions.explanation: A right-angled triangle has exactly one 90° angle. Two right angles would already total 180°, leaving no room for the third angle.

questions.question: An obtuse triangle has ___.
questions.explanation: An obtuse triangle has exactly one obtuse angle — an angle greater than 90°.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 50°, 60°, and 70°. What type is it by angles?
questions.explanation: All three angles (50°, 60°, 70°) are less than 90° → acute triangle. Check: 50+60+70 = 180° ✓

questions.question: A triangle has angles 30°, 60°, 90°. What type is it?
questions.explanation: One angle is exactly 90° → right-angled triangle.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 40°, 40°, and 100°. What type is it by angles?
questions.explanation: One angle (100°) is greater than 90° → obtuse triangle. Check: 40+40+100 = 180° ✓

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are 65° and 75°. The third angle is ___.
Can a triangle have two obtuse angles?
questions.explanation: No. Two obtuse angles each exceed 90°, so their sum alone would exceed 180° — impossible in a triangle.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle, by angles, is always ___.
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has all angles = 60°. Since all are less than 90°, it is always an acute triangle.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are 45° and 45°. The third angle is ___.
questions.explanation: Third angle = 180° − 45° − 45° = 90°. This triangle is a right-angled isosceles triangle.

questions.question: A triangle with angles 110°, 40°, 30° is ___.
questions.explanation: One angle (110°) exceeds 90° → obtuse triangle. Check: 110+40+30 = 180° ✓

questions.question: Which set of angles can form a valid triangle?
A triangle with one angle of 135° is ___.
questions.explanation: One angle (135°) is greater than 90° → obtuse triangle. E.g., 135°, 25°, 20° gives 180° ✓

questions.question: Third angle of a triangle when two angles are 30° and 60° is ___.
questions.explanation: Third angle = 180° − 30° − 60° = 90°. This is a right-angled triangle.
